inventory.$comment: DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE SECTION. In a real store this table lives in another system entirely (ERP, POS, a stock snapshot), not in the CMS that owns `products` above — and that split is the whole point: `availability` up there answers 'is this published and purchasable?', these numbers answer 'how many units exist?'. The demo data is arranged so every state shows up: (1) fieldbook-sketch-a5 is published as in_stock with ZERO units, the exact shape of an oversell; (2) CF-G09 is a catalogued variant with no inventory row, so it resolves to units:null = NOT VERIFIABLE, which blocks a write just like zero does; (3) roundhouse-detail-brush-set is out_of_stock in the catalog AND missing here, the only case where an unverifiable line may still raise a back-in-stock alert (the catalog confirms it independently); (4) fieldbook-sketch-a4 has 60 units under its SLUG and no row of its own under its SKU 'FB-A4', because the slug and the SKU are one pile — ordering 50 by slug and 50 by sku has to add up to 100 against 60, not fit twice; (5) everything else is a plain verified count.
